title: Scottish Open third round postponed due to fog
content:
The third round of the Scottish Open was postponed on Saturday due to fog.

Play was stopped twice due to haar — dense sea fog — at the Renaissance Club in North Berwick before it was confirmed the final group would not complete the third round due to the conditions.

Play was initially suspended at 10.45am BST (5.45am ET) before resuming at 1.10pm. The final group teed off at 6.15pm but could only finish seven holes before the fog returned, the horn sounded and play was stopped at around 8pm.

It will resume at 7am on Sunday, with Englishman Matt Fitzpatrick and Michael Thorbjornsen of the United States tied at the top on 11 under par but with their third rounds still to complete. American Johnny Keefer is the clubhouse leader at 10 under.

“The theme of links golf is being creative and being flexible, and understanding that things that are usually going to happen sometimes don’t,” Keefer added, in quotes carried by BBC Sport.

“And whether that’s a good shot or whether that’s just the weather, I think I had the mindset this week that anything can change, and I knew that it was going to be a little colder so I could kind of prep a little bit.”

Organisers confirmed the final round will not start before 10.15am on Sunday, with players teeing off from one tee.

Following the first delay, tournament director Miguel Vidaor explained in an interview with the European Tour’s in-house media: “We’ve had this haar from the word go.

“It’s been playable, marginal, but the rule is basically, players are not necessarily entitled to see the ball landing or the flag of the hole but for example, for a tee shot on a par four or five, they need to be able to see the contours of the bunkers or any penalty areas or the tree line.

“For an approach shot, it’s bunkers around the green and the pin flag. It’s been okay up until 10.20, the fog came a little bit thicker, especially on the higher parts of the golf course on holes five, six. and seven it became very thick to the point where it was not playable.”

World No. 2 Rory McIlroy had been among the leaders heading into round three but slipped to five under par on Saturday. Scottie Scheffler, the world No. 1, had missed his first cut in nearly four years on Friday.
